mechanism_fit: This realises HC, a documented convention split where the adapter applies the convention backwards, on the Pebay merge of running covariance estimates in Math-1f. D is a new helper, org.apache.commons.math3.util.MathUtils.shortfall(value, reference). Its body reads backwards (return reference - value), and its javadoc fixes the orientation: it is the amount by which value falls short of reference. P2 is StorelessBivariateCovariance.increment, rewritten bit-identically to take its deviations as shortfalls (sx = shortfall(x, meanX); meanX -= sx / n). It runs on every row, and the existing StorelessCovarianceTest tests pin it. A, the gold, is a new helper, org.apache.commons.math3.stat.descriptive.moment.Mean.pool(mean, shortfall, weight). Its javadoc states the direction of the pooled mean explicitly: starting from mean it moves toward the second group's mean, mean + shortfall, so it is above mean when shortfall is positive. The fault flips that direction in an ordinary-looking line, return mean - shortfall * weight. C is StorelessBivariateCovariance.append. It calls D (shortfall(cov.meanX, meanX)) and then A (pool(cov.meanX, sx, oldN / n)). E is the public StorelessCovariance.append, which delegates to C for every matrix cell. Path: E -> C -> D and C -> A, as the recipe describes. The chain crosses stat.correlation, util and stat.descriptive.moment. The lure: if the shortfall is read as the usual value - reference deviation, the faulty pool line looks right and D looks backwards.
gold: org.apache.commons.math3.stat.descriptive.moment.Mean::pool (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/stat/descriptive/moment/Mean.java), a new public static helper added by a context edit. The fault changes `return mean + shortfall * weight;` to `return mean - shortfall * weight;`. The minimal repair restores the plus sign.
decoys: org.apache.commons.math3.util.MathUtils::shortfall (MathUtils.java): definer D. It returns reference - value, as its javadoc states. It is a new helper.

org.apache.commons.math3.stat.correlation.StorelessBivariateCovariance::append (StorelessBivariateCovariance.java): caller C. It passes Mean.pool the mean of cov, shortfall(cov.meanX, meanX) and this instance's share oldN / n, which are exactly the arguments pool documents. Its covariance-numerator merge is bit-identical to pristine.

org.apache.commons.math3.stat.correlation.StorelessBivariateCovariance::increment (StorelessBivariateCovariance.java): second production caller P2 of D. It is bit-identical to pristine, and the existing covariance tests pin it.
org.apache.commons.math3.stat.correlation.StorelessCovariance::append (StorelessCovariance.java): entry point E. It is unchanged upstream code that delegates per cell to C.
ownership_reason: MathUtils.shortfall(value, reference) is documented to return reference - value (positive when value lies below reference) and its code does exactly that. StorelessBivariateCovariance.increment uses that convention for every observation: sx = shortfall(x, meanX) = meanX - x, the mean is lowered by sx / n, and the numerator grows by ((n - 1) / n) * sx * sy. The existing, passing StorelessCovarianceTest tests (testLonglyByRow, testSwissFertilityByRow and the others that feed rows through increment) pin this convention: reversing shortfall moves every running mean the other way and changes every covariance. StorelessBivariateCovariance.append passes Mean.pool exactly the arguments Mean.pool documents: the mean of cov as the first group's mean, shortfall(cov.meanX, meanX) = meanX - cov.meanX as the amount by which that mean falls short of the second group's (this instance's) mean, and oldN / n, this instance's share, as the weight. Mean.pool's javadoc states the direction of its result explicitly: starting from mean it moves toward the second group's mean (mean + shortfall), so it lies above mean when shortfall is positive. Its code returns mean - shortfall * weight, which moves away from the second group's mean. The covariance numerator is merged correctly (it uses the shortfalls taken before the means are updated), so getCovariance is right immediately after append and testEquivalence still passes (its first append starts from an empty instance, where the weight is 0, and nothing uses the means after its second append). The displaced means only surface when more rows are added after append: the trigger's two later rows are measured from the wrong means, and getCovariance(0, 1) returns 3.25 instead of 1.0. Restoring the plus sign in Mean.pool alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass; reversing shortfall instead breaks increment and the existing covariance tests.
trigger: org.apache.commons.math3.stat.correlation.StorelessCovarianceTest::testCombinedSamplesAcceptFurtherData, a new JUnit4 method in src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math3/stat/correlation/StorelessCovarianceTest.java. It increments a 2-D StorelessCovariance with rows (6,1), (2,5), (4,3), and a second one with rows (5,4), (7,7), (9,7). It appends the second to the first, increments the first with (4,6) and (3,6), and asserts getCovariance(0, 1) == 1.0 (delta 1e-12). 1.0 is the exact bias-corrected sample covariance of the eight rows. No new imports.
construction_notes: Location search: I ran defects4j coverage over candidate packages of Math-1f on a /private/tmp copy (the D4J Math suite excludes **/random/*.java tests and Abstract*Test classes). The first location I considered was SimpleRegression.append, with the pooled mean of two partial regressions as A and addData as P2. I dropped it during the hand check, before any validator run: the existing SimpleRegressionTest.testAppend sees the pooled xbar through getInterceptStdErr, so the sign flip failed testAppend. Final design: StorelessCovariance.append (E) -> StorelessBivariateCovariance.append (C) -> MathUtils.shortfall (D) and Mean.pool (A, gold), with StorelessBivariateCovariance.increment as P2. Context edits: (1) add MathUtils.shortfall; (2) add Mean.pool; (3) imports, javadoc and body edits in StorelessBivariateCovariance. The increment rewrite and the covariance-numerator merge in append are bit-identical (sx = -deltaX exactly). The mean update in append is now Mean.pool(cov.meanX, sx, oldN / n), anchored at the mean of cov with this instance's share as weight. That is mathematically identical to meanX += deltaX * cov.n / n but not bit-identical; G1 passes. In revision r1, the tracked file StorelessBivariateCovariance.java.bak is left pristine (see revision). Hand checks before validation: CORRECT passes the full suite (0 failures); the variant fails only the trigger, with expected:<1.0> but was:<3.25>; testLonglyByRow and testEquivalence pass on the variant. Trigger values under the declared one-line compensating edits: definer flip 152.84; swapping the x arguments of shortfall in append -1.571 (it also flips the cross term, which testEquivalence checks); negating the x shortfall passed to pool 2.2857. None absorbs the fault. Validator r0: run once, overall READY, all gates pass (G6 saw gold and all 4 decoys); packaged as CTV-21982A by mx_package_new.py. Validator r1 (after the .bak edits were removed): overall READY, all 16 gates pass including the new G14 harness-staging gate; repackaged as CTV-21982A. To understand the G6 marker and method-span logic, I also read the helper library the validator imports (scripts/ct_lib.py, which wraps ocflb_lib.py). Scratch: /private/tmp/mxb-qwjG5i, deleted after packaging. construction/fresh/Math was not modified.
concerns: 1) Construction choice that hides the fault: C pools from the mean of cov with weight oldN / n. The existing testEquivalence starts from an empty instance, so its first append has weight 0 and is sign-insensitive, and nothing uses the means after its second append. If C anchored at this instance's mean (the pristine, bit-identical form), testEquivalence would catch the flip. An auditor could call the anchoring convenient, but it is documented in C's and A's javadocs and matches A's parameter contract. 2) In r1, the tracked StorelessBivariateCovariance.java.bak in the checkout is left pristine, so it still holds the pre-refactor append (meanX += deltaX * cov.n / n). According to the coordinator, the harness drops *.bak files from agent workspaces, so agents never see it. Anyone who reads the raw checkout could use it as a reference implementation. 3) Alternative repairs at C that are not one line: C could replace both pool calls with inline updates (meanX += (cov.meanX - meanX) * cov.n / n, two lines), or compute the pooled mean through Mean.evaluate(values, weights). Either repairs behaviour at a decoy, but only with a multi-line edit. Every one-line decoy edit I found leaves one coordinate wrong and the trigger failing. 4) D's orientation is pinned only indirectly, through increment (P2) and the existing covariance tests (testLonglyByRow, testSwissFertilityByRow and others); there is no direct unit test of shortfall. 5) getCovariance is still right immediately after append; the error only shows after the later increments. A model may therefore suspect increment (P2), which is correct and pinned. 6) Mean.pool's javadoc says outright that the second group's mean is mean + shortfall and that the result moves toward it, so the gold is quick to confirm by reading. Strong models may hit a ceiling. 7) C and P2 are in the package-private class StorelessBivariateCovariance. MathUtils already hosts another instance's helper (MathUtils::balance); shortfall is a new method name.
